answers.why: Agent Platform Model Registry supports model versioning under a single model entry and movable aliases (e.g., 'approved', 'previous') to track release states natively without external spreadsheets or separate registry entries.

Agent Platform Inference supports autoscaling based on GPU duty cycle/utilization. Enabling this on the existing endpoint directly solves the bottleneck (high GPU usage, low CPU usage) with minimal operational overhead.

Registering retrained artifacts as new versions under the existing Model Registry entry and using version aliases (like 'production' and 'candidate') provides native lifecycle management and eliminates manual spreadsheet tracking.
To prevent training-serving skew and inconsistency across replicas, inference must reuse the exact normalization and encoding artifacts fitted during training, validated end-to-end from raw inputs.

Changes to preprocessing and postprocessing can subtly alter inputs and decisions. End-to-end benchmarking on labeled raw images in staging verifies both latency gains and preserved detection quality before production rollout.
Point-in-time joins on timestamped BigQuery history prevent data leakage (time travel) during training while leaving the online Agent Platform Feature Store serving path untouched.
Agent Platform Private Endpoints use Private Service Connect (PSC) to keep prediction traffic entirely within the private VPC network while retaining fully managed serving infrastructure.

Hardware selection requires empirical benchmarking across CPU, GPU, and TPU under realistic request patterns (single requests and bursts) to find the most cost-effective option that satisfies the p95 latency SLA.

For imbalanced fraud data, recall measures missed fraud (false negatives), whereas accuracy is misleading. Benchmarking throughput on target hardware alongside held-out recall directly addresses both business constraints.
Balancing model complexity against both validation error and online tail latency (via replayed app traffic in staging) directly optimizes accuracy within the production response-time SLA.
